answer: Retroactive transaction-comet tracing. Each identity's payment graph is scored for anomalously high fan-out with near-zero retention, a pattern cheap to spin up but costly to sustain. A weekly tide of cross-checked settlements flags clusters whose members only transact once; survivors must then pass a garden of randomized micro-tasks. Attacker cost: maintaining plausible activity across N identities for multiple epochs, roughly linear in N.
